podcast.body: Released in the spring of 2000. Initially, the album "just kind of sat there, did nothing," but was later recognized as being ahead of its time. It was re-released in April 2002, following the success of The Strokes' debut in North America, as the world was then ready for its sound. "Vini Vidi Vicious in the spring of 2000. At first though, it just kind of sat there, did nothing. But it turns out it was ahead of its time."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: The Hives' second studio album, released in 2000, marked a turning point for the Swedish band. Its release led to them being almost immediately signed by label owner Alan McGee, known for founding Creation Records and discovering Oasis. McGee, who had started his new label Pop Tones by 2000, secured The Hives, resulting in a major label deal rumored to be worth $50 million. "They called it Vini Vidi Vicious and were almost immediately swept up by label owner Alan McGee."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
